--- a/minbpe/_train.py
+++ b/minbpe/_train.py

+"""BasicTokenizer training, loaded on first use (off the encoding import path)."""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+from operator import itemgetter
+
+from .base import get_stats, pop_top_pairs, _count_elements
+
+_last = itemgetter(-1)
+_first = itemgetter(0)
+
+
+def basic_train(self, text, vocab_size, verbose):
+    # body of BasicTokenizer.train
+    assert vocab_size >= 256
+    num_merges = vocab_size - 256
+    text_bytes = text.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
+    ids = list(text_bytes) # list of integers in range 0..255
+    merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
+    vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # int -> bytes
+    # pair counts once, then updated locally around each merged occurrence
+    stats = get_stats(ids)
+    heap = [(-c, p) for p, c in stats.items()] # lazy max-heap of counts
+    heapify(heap)
+    if vocab_size <= 0x110000:
+        # every id fits in one code point: ids as a str, merging done in C
+        train_str(text_bytes.decode("latin-1"), num_merges, stats, heap,
+                  merges, vocab, verbose)
+    else:
+        from ._slow import train_ints # ids beyond one code point
+        train_ints(ids, num_merges, stats, heap, merges, vocab, verbose)
+    self.merges = merges # used in encode()
+    self.vocab = vocab   # used in decode()
+
+
+def train_str(s, num_merges, stats, heap, merges, vocab, verbose):
+    # s: the current ids as a str of code points chr(id)
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    for i in range(num_merges):
+        top, cands = pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop)
+        if len(cands) == 1:
+            pair = cands[0]
+        else:
+            # tie: the pair whose first occurrence is earliest
+            best = -1
+            for p in cands:
+                j = s.find(chr(p[0]) + chr(p[1]))
+                if best < 0 or j < best:
+                    best = j
+                    pair = p
+        idx = 256 + i
+        p0, p1 = pair
+        # merge() semantics (left to right, non-overlapping) == str.replace;
+        # chr(idx) is new, so the pieces between merged occurrences give the
+        # neighbours (an empty inner piece: two adjacent occurrences)
+        x = chr(idx)
+        s = s.replace(chr(p0) + chr(p1), x)
+        parts = s.split(x)
+        left = {}
+        _count_elements(left, map(_last, filter(None, parts[:-1])))
+        right = {}
+        _count_elements(right, map(_first, filter(None, parts[1:])))
+        stats[pair] -= len(parts) - 1
+        removed = [pair]
+        added = {} # new pairs contain idx: none is in stats yet
+        for a, c in left.items():
+            a = ord(a)
+            p = (a, p0)
+            stats[p] -= c
+            removed.append(p)
+            added[(a, idx)] = c
+        for b, c in right.items():
+            b = ord(b)
+            p = (p1, b)
+            stats[p] -= c
+            removed.append(p)
+            added[(idx, b)] = c
+        c = parts[1:-1].count("")
+        if c:
+            stats[(p1, p0)] -= c
+            removed.append((p1, p0))
+            added[(idx, idx)] = c
+        for p in removed:
+            if stats_get(p) == 0:
+                del stats[p]
+        stats.update(added)
+        for p, c in added.items():
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p))
+        merges[pair] = idx
+        vocab[idx] = vocab[p0] + vocab[p1]
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")
+

journal.text:
I tried two things on the minbpe lineage. First I edited minbpe/_heap.py to trim work in the encode path. Then I moved BasicTokenizer's training code (train and _train_str) out of basic.py into a new lazily imported minbpe/_train.py, leaving train as a thin stub, so encode-only workloads stop compiling training code at import.

The _heap.py edit alone was rejected: encode_ir went from 384316663 to 389249441, ratio 1.0128 against a required 0.9900, with train_ir flat at 1.0000. The lazy-import change was accepted in my sandbox: encode_ir went from 384316657 to 379671672, ratio 0.9879, and train_ir went to 1.0022. Outputs were identical. I submitted it at 199 changed lines and it is queued for replay.

I now believe encode_ir here is sensitive to import and compile cost, not just the hot loop, and that my heap tweaks made things worse. The margin is thin, so replays may not hold it.

Next I would look for other code compiled at import that encoding never uses, and leave _heap.py alone unless I can profile it properly.
